turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: You will not say such things and leave me to worry about the future, O-lan! Our son is a strong man and will make his own way, and I will not have you burdening me with these fears.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: I have prepared the sweet rice dish, Grandmother, just as you instructed, with full measure of lard and sugar, and the eight fruits are arranged in the center. May I pour you a cup of wine?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: You must see that the maid is well cared for, that she has a fine dowry and a good home when she marries my son.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: Thank you, Grandmother, I am grateful for your consideration, but I am not worthy of a fine dowry or a good home, I am but a humble servant.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: I will not have you talking of marrying and settling my son so soon, O-lan. You must rest and think of nothing but your health, not of the future.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I must die, Wang Lung, and I want to see my son settled before I go. It is not for me to worry about my own health, but for me to think of my family's future.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: I am but a humble servant, Grandmother, and I do not wish to burden your son with marriage and family responsibilities, especially in these difficult times.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: You must not think of this now, O-lan, you must think of yourself and getting well, not of marrying off our son like he's a piece of property to be sold!

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I will not think of my own health, Wang Lung, but of my son's future, and I want this good maid to be his wife, she is kind and helpful, and she serves me well.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Why must you be so stubborn, O-lan? Can you not see how this troubles me, how it weighs on my mind to think of you leaving us so soon?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I will see our son wedded to this good maid, and then I will die easily, knowing his future is secure.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: I beg of you, Grandmother, please do not think of me as a suitable match for your son. I am but a lowly servant, unworthy of your son's love and respect.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: Mother, please do not worry about me, I will be fine, and I will marry whoever you think best for me, I just want to make you happy before you go.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: You are not listening to me, O-lan. I will not have you worrying about our son's future now, when all that matters is your own health and well-being.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I will not rest until our son is married and settled, Wang Lung. It is the only way I can be at peace, knowing his future is secure.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: You must not exhaust yourself with such thoughts, O-lan. Your health is all that matters to me.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I will not rest, Wang Lung, until I see our son's face shine with happiness, and this good maid's hands bring him children to inherit our land.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: I promise, Mother, I will make you proud and give you no more cause for worry. I will choose a good wife and start a family, just as you wish.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: I will see this good maid as a daughter to me, and help her to care for my son, so that he may be strong and healthy, and his children may grow and thrive.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: Do not worry about me, Mother. I am strong and healthy, and I will take care of myself and start a new family. I promise to make you proud.
